1_id_category: r3s3_lf_value-B2 / lf_value / row-efficiency law of the coverage channel — knee, HF-row exchange rate and the alignment mediator, under an arm-invariant scaler, with the forward-sensitive ch subpopulation stratified
2_motivation: B1 answered *what* LF-at-train is worth on the honest panel — the value is entirely the supply of distinct condition rows (E_cov/E_total ∈ [0.972, 1.024] on 30/30 cells; A2_lf_covered is the *same learned function* as A0_nolf, D(A2,A1)/D(A0,A1) ≥ 1.007 on 5/5 cells) — and left *what it costs* completely unmeasured: two points on ch (10 conditions → 7–44 % recovery; 395 → 97–102 %) with nothing between, and one HF-budget point (4× the HF budget buys 8–59 % of the LF pool). The websearcher's C1 verdict fixes exactly what may and may not be claimed: "**The LF-count sweep genre is published — do not claim it.** ... **The finding must be the measured knee and exchange rate, never the sweep.**" This card therefore delivers the knee, the exchange rate and — the part nothing retrieved does — the **mediating learned quantity** that makes it a law rather than a table ("nothing retrieved reports a mediating learned quantity for MF sample-count curves"; iteration 2 term 1 returned **nothing** for "effective sample size / exchange rate" in MF surrogacy). It occupies the seam the survey itself certifies is empty: mapping-family MF surrogates must "first run the low-fidelity simulator" at every new input (2408.17075 Eq. 13) and mapping/corrective families "are not able to take advantage" of n2 > n1 at all — our ladder consumes extra LF rows *and* discards LF at test by construction. Three further things are folded in at zero extra training cost: (i) the **repair B1's own part 7 demanded** — `per_rung_max` is computed over the rows an arm keeps (`smoke_eval.py:491-495`), so on ch the full-pool arms trained at s_rung/s_hf = 1.169–1.174 against the 5-row arms' 1.000, which would have made a cap ladder partly a normalisation curve and which leaves B1's own ch decomposition confounded at ~17 %; (ii) the **A2_lf_covered control re-certified** under the fixed scaler, which the C2 verdict names as the claimable object ("no retrieved work runs an LF arm restricted to *already-HF-covered* inputs"); (iii) the **forward-sensitive ch subpopulation** (r3s1-B1 T3c: 27 seed-invariant rows, 0.4476 σ condition gap, nnd ratio 1.0176, nearest-train-field rel-L2 ratio 3.29) stratified per-row on the same dumps — the C3 verdict's "most defensible novelty", delivered as a certified measurement, with the terminology hazard discharged by naming and defining it inline and banning "non-identifiable" from the card. `ifc_poisson` is dropped on B1's evidence (exactly affine, oracle residual 2.9e-08; `affine_on_hf_train` 0.057375 unbeaten; rung→HF transfer 3.15–81.2), and no distillation, teacher, pretrain→finetune or auxiliary-target arm is proposed (all `preempted (cite)` or certified null).
3_description:
New family `models_r3/r3s3_row_efficiency`, vendored **byte-for-byte** from `models_r3/r3s3_lf_channels` @ `050806e0` (backbone width 64 / 4 blocks / `pinned_min_rung_nyquist` modes cap 12, AdamW 1e-3 / wd 1e-5 / cosine / clip 1.0, `steps = epochs × 25`, HF batch 5 / LF batch 16, `_step_rng(seed, step)` resume contract) with exactly four changes, each with a provenance comment:
1. **`R3S3B2_SCALER=per_rung_max_fullpool`** (NEW): `max|y|` per rung computed over the **full rung pool of the stripped train view**, independent of arm and cap, with a hard assert that the scaler is bit-identical across every arm/cap of a (dataset, rung) pair and a recorded `s_rung/s_hf` table per leg. This is B1 part 7 requirement (1).
2. **`A3c_lf_uncov_cap`** — the ladder arm: `LF_COND_SET=uncovered`, `LF_COND_CAP=c`, per-rung cap draw `np.sort(np.random.default_rng([split_seed, fid]).permutation(n_uncov)[:min(c, n_uncov)])` (B1's own recorded draw convention, unchanged). ch ladder `c ∈ {5,10,20,40,80,160,395}` over 2 rungs (395 uncovered/rung); ifc_heat ladder `c ∈ {1,2,5,10,15,45,95}` clipped per rung to the nested uncovered counts 95/45/15 at rungs 8/16/32. Every leg's `lf_row_manifest` records **both** `n_rows` and `n_distinct_conditions` (they differ: ch ≈ 2c until saturation, ifc_heat sub-additive because the ladder is nested), and the ladder is plotted against `n_distinct_conditions`, the causal axis B1's mechanism names.
3. **`A5_hf_budget_nolf`** (ch only) — `N_HF ∈ {10,20,40}`, `LF_COND_SET=none`, HF batch held at 5, rows drawn from the already-shipped 400 by B1's recorded rule. ifc_heat is native N_hf = 5 and gets no HF ladder; **the exchange rate is declared a ch-only deliverable**.
4. **Per-leg mediator + stratified emission**: condition-response alignment and amplitude per leg (`tools/response_decomposition.py` conventions), and per-row scored rel-L2 dumps split by the **forward-sensitive** mask — imported verbatim from `worktrees/r3s1_factorised/B1/scratchpad/turn3_results.json::t3c_hard_rows.hard_mask` (100-element 0/1, 27 ones) **and** independently re-derived model-free as the top-27 ch test rows by nearest-train-HF-field rel-L2, with the overlap reported and both stratifications published if they disagree.

Arms: `A0_nolf`, `A1_lf_all` (recovery denominator), `A2_lf_covered` (C2 control), `A3c_lf_uncov_cap` (ladder), `A5_hf_budget_nolf` (ch only). Condition-only at test on the stripped view; LF never enters the test path. Grid **per training seed**: ch 39 legs (7 caps × 3 HF draws = 21; A0/A1/A2 × 3 draws = 9; HF ladder 3 × 3 draws = 9) + ifc_heat 10 legs (7 caps + A0/A1/A2) + 1 guard leg (`heat_local`, epochs 2) = **50 legs**; 3 SLURM jobs, one per training seed, **150 legs total**. At B1's measured 2.4 min/leg (60 legs in 140.1–150.3 min, `state/timing_ledger.json`) ≈ 2.0 h/job; `--time 05:00:00`, `--mail-user=ezeng@caltech.edu --mail-type=END,FAIL`. Blocking pre-flights: scaler arm-invariance assert, `R3S3B2_DATA_BINDING_ASSERT` tying `copylf_baselines.json` to `floors.json`, floor seam at 1e-9, and `tools/stale_checkpoint_audit.py --fail-on-stale` on this card's own outputs before scoring. All ch statements reference-free (ADR r3-0003 D2, MDD 1.7077); every ifc_heat number reports `affine_on_hf_train` = 0.070918 beside it (program §2).
4_expected_result:
- **D-A knee (ch, primary).** R rises from ≈0.07–0.44 at cap 5 (10 distinct conditions — B1's measured A3s range) to 0.97–1.02 at cap 395, roughly logarithmic in distinct conditions. Predicted knee **c\* ∈ {40, 80}** (80–160 distinct conditions), i.e. mean R(80) ≥ 0.90 with R(40) ≈ 0.75–0.90 and R(20) ≈ 0.55–0.75. **Δ vs anchor**: none claimed on the panel geomean — the own-stream anchor `r2s3_lf_train_signal-B3` (11.1689 [10.9988, 11.3390]) is a scoring reference the A1 legs are only expected to *reproduce* (B1's post-repair seam: −0.75..+0.10 %/seed); the deliverable is the curve, not a score win. **vs noise floor**: rung-to-rung R gaps of 0.10–0.20 against a floor width of **0.020–0.029 R units** (`tau_rel` 0.36124864423263325 skill × 0.041802962686225575 = 0.015101 nRMSE, over an A0→A1 effect of 0.514–0.743 nRMSE) ⇒ **3.4–10× the certified floor**.
- **D-A ifc_heat (secondary).** R(1) ≈ 0.2–0.5, R(15) ≥ 0.8, R(95) ≈ 1.0; declared coarse because `tau_rel` 0.1640195793751628 × 0.074 = 0.012137 nRMSE = **21.8 %** of the 0.055669 effect, so only steps ≥ 0.22 R are resolvable.
- **D-B floor-crossing cap.** On ch, expected between cap 5 and cap 20: A0_nolf (≈1.05–1.28 nRMSE) is worse than `zero` (1.0) and `nn_condition` (0.96901), so the ladder must cross 0.96901 before any recovery is useful. On ifc_heat the gate is non-binding (A0 0.060518 already beats `nn_condition` 0.10316 and `affine_on_hf_train` 0.070918) — that asymmetry is itself a reportable result.
- **D-C exchange rate (ch only).** From B1's single point (N_hf 20 = 8–59 % of the LF pool) the predicted bracket is **1 HF row ≈ 8–40 uncovered LF condition rows per rung**, tightened to a ladder-bracketed interval at three recovery levels; expected to be non-constant (cheaper per LF row at low caps).
- **D-D mediator collapse.** Pooled Pearson(R, alignment) ≥ 0.95 (B1 measured 0.985 within the LF arms); HF-budget points expected to land on the same curve within 0.05 R.
- **D-E stratification.** R_hard(c) expected to lag R_easy(c) by 0.05–0.25 at intermediate caps, i.e. the forward-sensitive rows are predicted to need a **larger** cap than the bulk; a lag above 0.029 R clears the ch floor.
- **D-F re-certified decomposition.** Under `per_rung_max_fullpool`, ch/ifc_heat A2_lf_covered recovery expected in **[−0.05, +0.10]**, confirming B1's E_cov/E_total ∈ [0.972, 1.024] on a matched procedure.
expected_falsification: FALSIFIED if either (i) the ch recovery curve carries **no knee resolvable at the certified floor** — no ladder rung c\* with mean R(c\*) ≥ 0.90 whose next-lower rung is lower by more than 0.030 in R units (= 2× `tau_rel`(ch) = 2 × 0.36124864423263325 skill × 0.041802962686225575 = 0.030202 nRMSE, i.e. 4.1–5.9 % of the measured A0→A1 effect of 0.514–0.743 nRMSE), so that R is within one floor width of log-linear in distinct conditions across the whole 10→395 range and the "affordable knee" claim dies; or (ii) under the arm-invariant `per_rung_max_fullpool` scaler **A2_lf_covered recovers R ≥ 0.25** on `sharp__cahn_hilliard` or `ifc_heat` (8.5–12.3× `tau_rel` on ch; 1.15× `tau_rel`(ifc_heat) = 0.1640195793751628 skill × 0.074 = 0.012137 nRMSE against a 0.055669 effect), which would invert batch 1's headline that the coverage channel is the entire effect and reassign part of it to optimisation — with two pre-registered secondary predictions that are reported but do not alone falsify: the HF-budget legs collapsing onto the LF ladder's R(alignment) curve within 0.05 R (failure ⇒ the exchange rate is published as a bracketed table, not a law), and ifc_heat reaching R ≥ 0.78 at some cap below its full 95-row pool (failure ⇒ ifc_heat is reported as an unresolved corroboration only, per its 21.8 %-of-effect floor width).

prior_art.verdict_quoted:
> | **C1** — **row-efficiency law**: sweep the number of *distinct uncovered* LF condition rows (5→395) on ch + ifc_heat at 3 seeds; report recovery vs row count **and vs measured response alignment**; derive an LF-row ↔ HF-row exchange rate against `A4_hf20_nolf` | **preempted-but-MF-composition-open** | Kirby et al., *Data-driven modelling of turbine wake interactions*, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2301.01699 (fetched: HF fixed at 50, LF ∈ {250, 500, 1000}, MAE 1.46/0.828/0.866 %, explicit saturation "because the number of high-fidelity training points is fixed"). Functional-output benchmark grid: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.17075 (fetched: n1={2,5,10}×dim(U), n2={1,5,10}×n1, 9 combos × 10 DoE repetitions, >12 MF surrogates). | The **LF-count sweep genre is published — do not claim it.** Open, simultaneously: (a) LF **absent from the test path by construction** — the survey's mapping family must "first run the low-fidelity simulator" at each new input (Eq. 13), and mapping/corrective families "are not able to take advantage" of n2 > n1 at all; (b) the sweep is over **distinct conditions**, with the covered/uncovered split held fixed (A2 control), not over raw snapshot count; (c) **N_hf = 5** with a certified `tau_rel` (ch 0.3612, ifc_heat 0.1640) and reference-free reporting; (d) the sweep is regressed on a **mediating learned quantity** (condition-response alignment, r = 0.985), not just error; (e) a numeric **exchange rate** vs a matched HF-budget arm — iteration 2 term 1 returned **nothing** for "effective sample size / exchange rate" in MF surrogacy. The finding must be the measured knee and exchange rate, never the sweep. |

> | **C2** — **LF as identifiability supply (distinct condition rows) vs LF as function prior / optimisation aid**, proved by the A2_lf_covered control and the E_cov/E_total decomposition | **preempted-but-MF-composition-open** (the *mechanism sentence* is preempted outright) | Kim et al., *Data-efficient multi-fidelity training for high-fidelity MLIPs*, https://arxiv.org/html/2409.07947v1 (fetched, verbatim: "geometric and compositional spaces **not covered by the high-fidelity** meta-GGA database **can be effectively inferred from low-fidelity GGA data**"; also "more effective than transfer learning or Δ-learning"). Coverage framing: https://arxiv.org/html/2402.17061v1 (fetched: "multi-fidelity data provide broad coverage of the admissible parameter space, while high-fidelity samples are more sparsely distributed"). Batch-1 D2 vocabulary (statistical-to-computational gap) carried forward: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.04282. | **"LF helps by covering what HF does not cover" is published prose — quote it, never present it as this stream's insight.** What is open is the **discriminating control**: no retrieved work runs an LF arm restricted to *already-HF-covered* inputs (our A2), and therefore none can attribute the effect to supply rather than to procedure/regularisation/warm start. Also open: the quantitative decomposition E_cov/E_total = [0.972, 1.024] on 30/30 cells with E_opt ≈ 0, and the claim that the covered-only arm is *the same learned function* as the no-LF arm. Additional caution: "LF labels at new inputs" is externally just **semi-supervised regression with cheap biased pseudo-labels** (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2408.07221, search-return only) — use that name, don't invent one. |

> | **C3** — **hard non-identifiable subpopulation**: detect the seed-invariant 27-row ch subset (conditions within 0.448 σ of training, fields 3.29× farther) and show LF-at-train specifically repairs it (92 of A0's worse-than-zero rows, 97 % of the pair's gain) | **preempted-but-MF-composition-open**, leaning novel-composition (nearest neighbours are all in adjacent problems) | Nearest neighbour 1 — NO failure diagnosis under **structured shift**, not in-distribution subpopulations: https://arxiv.org/html/2601.11428 (fetched: "strong in-distribution accuracy does not reliably predict robustness"; 750 models, 5 PDE families). Nearest neighbour 2 — the identifiability vocabulary is the **inverse direction**: https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1013553 (fetched: "Non-influential parameters are considered 'practically non-identifiable' in that they have little to no impact on the model output"). Search-snippet only: NO test-error outliers attributed to "limited diversity and size of the training dataset" (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14475). | Nothing retrieved defines an **in-distribution** hard mask by an input-close/output-far ratio, checks its **seed invariance**, or attributes an MF gain to it. That composition is the most defensible novelty in this batch — but it is a **diagnostic**, so it must be delivered as a certified measurement (per-row deltas vs the ch reference-free convention), not as a method. **Terminology hazard (blocking for the card):** "non-identifiable" in the literature means *parameters that barely move the output*; our mask is the opposite (conditions that barely move but outputs that move a lot = local ill-conditioning / high forward sensitivity). Round-2 §12's "unidentifiable phrasing rule" bites here — define the term in-card on first use or rename it (e.g. *forward-sensitive* / *response-amplifying* subpopulation). |

NEW in this card: (1) the arm-invariant scaler mode per_rung_max_fullpool plus its invariance assert (B1 part 7 requirement 1 - per_rung_max is currently computed over the rows an arm keeps, smoke_eval.py:491-495, giving s_rung/s_hf 1.169-1.174 on ch full-pool arms vs 1.000 on 5-row arms); (2) the ladder arm A3c_lf_uncov_cap driven by R3S3B2_LF_COND_CAP; (3) the HF-budget ladder arm A5_hf_budget_nolf (ch only, already-shipped rows, the axis B1's A4_hf20_nolf already used); (4) per-leg alignment/amplitude emission and per-row stratified dumps. env._note: keys prefixed _ are card directives, NOT passed to --env. The --env set is exactly the 36 R3S3B2_* keys above; each leg overrides only R3S3B2_ARM, R3S3B2_SPLIT_SEED, R3S3B2_LF_COND_SET, R3S3B2_LF_COND_CAP and R3S3B2_N_HF (the guard leg also sets epochs=2). ARM<->selector binding, asserted in smoke_eval, MUST raise on any other combination: A0_nolf=(N_HF 5, COND_SET none, CAP 0); A1_lf_all=(5, all, 0); A2_lf_covered=(5, covered, 0); A3c_lf_uncov_cap=(5, uncovered, CAP in the dataset's ladder); A5_hf_budget_nolf=(N_HF in {10,20,40}, none, 0, ch only).
env._grid: PER TRAINING SEED (3 seeds -> 3 SLURM jobs, 150 legs total). sharp__cahn_hilliard, 39 legs: A3c at CAP in {5,10,20,40,80,160,395} x SPLIT_SEED in {0,1,2} = 21; A0_nolf/A1_lf_all/A2_lf_covered x SPLIT_SEED in {0,1,2} = 9; A5_hf_budget_nolf at N_HF in {10,20,40} x SPLIT_SEED in {0,1,2} = 9. ifc_heat, 10 legs (native N_hf=5, SPLIT_SEED=native): A3c at CAP in {1,2,5,10,15,45,95} = 7; A0/A1/A2 = 3. Plus 1 guard leg (heat_local, epochs 2, arm A1_lf_all). NO ifc_poisson leg (B1 part 7 requirement 2) and NO sharp__phase_field_crystal_2d leg (report-only, ADR r3-0004).
env._cap_semantics: CAP is PER RUNG, extending B1's own convention (A3s_lf_uncov_n5 = 5 covered-matched rows at every rung). Draw: np.sort(np.random.default_rng([split_seed, fid]).permutation(n_uncov_rung)[:min(CAP, n_uncov_rung)]) - a pure function of the leg, independent of training. ch has 2 LF rungs with 395 uncovered conditions each, so CAP c supplies 2c rows and approximately 2c distinct conditions until saturation at 395 (CAP 395 = 790 rows, 395 distinct = the A3_lf_uncovered arm of B1). ifc_heat's ladder is NESTED (rung 32's 20 conditions subset rung 16's 50 subset rung 8's 100; uncovered 95/45/15), so distinct conditions are SUB-ADDITIVE across rungs. EVERY leg must record n_rows AND n_distinct_conditions in lf_row_manifest, and all curves are plotted against n_distinct_conditions.
env._hf_subset_draws: SPLIT_SEED in {0,1,2} draws N_HF of the 400 ch HF train rows via np.sort(np.random.default_rng(s).permutation(400)[:N_HF]) - IDENTICAL to B1 and r2s3-B3, so the A0/A1/A2 legs at N_HF=5 form an exact reproduction seam against B1 (which reproduces the fresh anchor to -0.75..+0.10 %/seed post-repair). At N_HF=5: d0 = 55,88,133,202,293; d1 = 39,45,51,198,379; d2 = 11,157,162,211,355. A5 legs at N_HF in {10,20,40} use the same generator with the same k-prefix rule (nested draws) and hold HF_BATCH at 5 so the gradient shape is matched across the HF ladder.
env._scaler_fix: per_rung_max_fullpool = max|y| over ALL rows of that rung in the stripped TRAIN view (not the arm's kept rows), computed once per (dataset, rung) and cached. R3S3B2_SCALER_INVARIANCE_ASSERT=1 requires smoke_eval to recompute the scaler for each leg and raise unless it is bit-identical to the cached value, and to record s_rung, s_hf and s_rung/s_hf in the result JSON. RATIONALE (B1 part 6 turn 2): the cap ladder varies exactly the rows the old scaler was computed over, so the old rule would make the cap curve partly a normalisation curve; measured on ch as 1.169-1.174 (A1/A3) vs 1.000 (A2/A3s), and on the dropped ifc_poisson as 0.982-1.636. This also discharges round-2 report section 6's arm-comparison mis-specification warning ('compare at matched rows and matched procedure').
env._deliverables: D-A knee: R(c) = (nRMSE(A0) - nRMSE(arm@c)) / (nRMSE(A0) - nRMSE(A1_lf_all)), reference-free, aggregated over the 9 cells per cap on ch (3 HF draws x 3 training seeds) and 3 cells per cap on ifc_heat. D-B floor-crossing cap: smallest cap whose scored nRMSE beats the dataset's best training-free floor. D-C exchange rate (ch ONLY): the LF-cap bracket whose mean R matches R at N_HF in {10,20,40}, each bracket priced against tau_rel. D-D single-mediator collapse: pooled Pearson/Spearman of R on measured condition-response alignment across LF-cap AND HF-budget cells, plus the residual of the HF points about the LF-ladder fit. D-E forward-sensitive stratification (ch): R_hard(c) vs R_easy(c) on the 27/73 split. D-F re-certified decomposition: E_cov/E_total and E_opt under the fixed scaler, replacing B1's scaler-confounded ch figure.
env._hard_mask: Import t3c_hard_rows.hard_mask (100 elements, 27 ones) from R3S3B2_HARD_MASK_JSON AFTER asserting split identity (ch n_test == 100 and the condition-matrix hash matches r3s1-B1's). Because that mask was derived from r3s1's own per-row rel-L2 bimodality (model-dependent), ALSO re-derive a model-free mask = top-27 ch test rows by nearest-train-HF-field relative-L2 distance, report the overlap, and publish the stratification under BOTH masks if they disagree. TERMINOLOGY (blocking, websearcher C3 + round-2 section 6 phrasing rule): call it the FORWARD-SENSITIVE subpopulation, defined inline on first use as 'condition-space-indistinguishable (max per-dim standardised gap 0.4476 sigma, nearest-train-neighbour ratio 1.0176) but field-distant (nearest-train-field rel-L2 ratio 3.29)'. The words non-identifiable / unidentifiable are BANNED from this card - the literature uses them for the opposite meaning (PLOS pcbi.1013553).
env._reporting_discipline: ch is REFERENCE-FREE (ADR r3-0003 D2, MDD 1.7077): report nRMSE ratios and R, never a ch copy-LF skill delta. Every ifc_heat number is reported next to affine_on_hf_train = 0.070918 (program section 2 affine-floor rule) and its paper bar 0.074. Prior-art clause on the card MUST carry: the survey's mapping family must 'first run the low-fidelity simulator' at every new input (2408.17075 Eq. 13) and mapping/corrective families 'are not able to take advantage' of n2 > n1 - our arms consume extra LF rows and discard LF at test. The LF-count-sweep genre is Kirby 2301.01699 and the (n1,n2) field-output grid is 2408.17075: cite them, claim only the knee, the exchange rate and the mediator. 'LF helps by covering what HF does not cover' is Kim 2409.07947 verbatim - quote it, never present it as this stream's insight; the claimable object is the A2_lf_covered control. Name the external genre: semi-supervised regression with cheap biased pseudo-labels.

CARDED CHANGE 1 (arm-invariant scaler). R3S3B2_SCALER=per_rung_max_fullpool: `_fullpool_scaler(train, fid)` = max(|y| over ALL rows of that rung in the stripped TRAIN view, 1e-12) — for the HF rung too, i.e. over all HF train rows and NOT the N_hf draw, which is what makes s_rung/s_hf a pure (dataset, rung) constant across the cap ladder AND the HF-budget ladder. The signature takes no arm/cap/selection argument, so no future edit can leak the treatment into the normalisation. R3S3B2_SCALER_INVARIANCE_ASSERT=1 recomputes it per leg under every alternative selection (all/covered/uncovered rows, the full cap ladder, the arm's own kept rows) and RAISES unless every value is bit-identical (float64 ==); s_rung, s_hf, s_rung/s_hf and arm_rows_max_over_fullpool (B1's confound number) are recorded in every result JSON. The base rules per_rung_max / shared_max_all_rungs remain selectable and are labelled arm_dependent so B1's confound can be reproduced deliberately.
